10 Gallon Tote.blurb: The workhorse of my worm setup. A simple, stackable tote with a lid keeps worms contained and makes moving or splitting bins easy.

Blue Tarp.blurb: Heavy-duty ground cover for outdoor piles. Keeps rain out of the active zone while still letting air move through the sides.

Bus Boy Tubs.blurb: Food-service tubs are my go-to worm bin containers: cheap, durable, and easy to drill ventilation holes into. I keep a stack of them for splitting bins.

KN95 Masks.blurb: Dry bedding and turning hot piles kick up dust. A KN95 keeps it out of my lungs when I'm working with carbon materials.

Pine Shavings.blurb: My primary carbon-rich bedding for worm bins. Unscented shavings absorb moisture well and give the worms a loose, aerated bed to live in.

Waterproof gloves.blurb: Worm bins are wet work. These keep my hands dry and clean when I'm digging through castings or mixing bedding.

Urban Worm Bag.blurb: A self-contained worm bin for apartments and small spaces. No drilling, no mess: feed it from the top and harvest castings when ready.

Vermibag.blurb: Another bag-style worm bin I've used for smaller setups. Great option if you want vermicomposting without a dedicated tub or stand.

Bug Zapper.blurb: A 2800V electric zapper for the kitchen. Fruit flies and gnats are attracted to the light and knocked out before they reach the food.

Diatomaceous Earth Food Grade.blurb: A fine powder that dehydrates crawling insects. I dust it around bin lids and entry points as a physical fly barrier. Food grade is the only kind to use around food.

Mosquito Bits Bti.blurb: Granules of Bt (Bacillus thuringiensis israelensis) for standing water. Drops into any puddle or container to stop mosquito larvae without harming beneficial insects.

Mosquito Dunks.blurb: The disc version of the same Bt treatment. One dunk in a bucket or rain barrel keeps mosquito larvae from hatching all season.

Sticky Fly Trap.blurb: A simple glue-board trap for the kitchen. I hang one near the bin whenever fruit flies show up and it takes them out fast.

5 Gallon Bucket and Gamma Seal Lid.blurb: My bokashi vessel. The gamma seal lid is the key: it makes the bucket truly airtight so fermentation stays anaerobic and odor-free.

Bokashi Bran.blurb: Inoculated grain for bokashi. A handful on every layer feeds the beneficial microbes that break down food scraps in the bucket.

100 Pack Utility Knife Blades.blurb: Spare blades for my paper prep. I cut cardboard and paper into small pieces before they go in the bin so they break down faster.

Bonsaii 12 Sheet Micr-cut Paper Shredder.blurb: Shreds up to 12 sheets at a time into micro-cuts. The fine pieces decompose quickly in both worm bins and hot piles.

Folding Utility Knife.blurb: My everyday cutting tool for cardboard, paper, and trimming. The folding body keeps it safe to carry around the yard.

Canon EF-S 24mm f/2.8 STM Lens.blurb: My pancake lens for B-roll and tight shots of bins and close-ups. Light enough to carry on every shoot.

Canon EOS 90D.blurb: My main camera for the channel. 32MP stills and solid 4K video make it a do-everything workhorse.

Davinci Resolve.blurb: My editing and color-grading suite. The free version has everything I need to cut, grade, and export the channel's videos.

Fujifilm X-T5.blurb: My mirrorless backup camera. 40MP and the film simulations give footage a distinct look without heavy grading.

GEEKOTO Tripd.blurb: A flexible tripod that bends into awkward positions. Perfect for low angles inside bins or mounting in tight spots where a normal tripod won't fit.

GoPro Hero 8 Black.blurb: My action cam for in-bin footage and timelapses. The stabilization makes handheld pile-turning shots usable, and it's small enough to mount anywhere.

Neewer Advanced 660 LED Studio Lighting.blurb: My studio lighting kit for talking-head segments. Softboxes keep the light even and flattering without expensive pro gear.

Panasonic 4k Camcorder.blurb: A dedicated camcorder for long-form recording sessions. The built-in zoom covers wide yard shots without swapping lenses.

Chapin Sprayer.blurb: My garden sprayer for watering piles and applying compost tea. A reliable hand-pump design that's easy to clean between uses.

Ego 4 Gallon Sprayer.blurb: Cordless sprayer for bigger jobs. The battery power means no pumping when I'm treating a whole bed or watering multiple piles.

Meme's Worms.blurb: My go-to supplier for red wiggler worms. Healthy, active worms that arrive fast and establish in new bins quickly.

FoodCycler Eco 3.blurb: Entry-level electric composter with a 3-liter bucket. Ideal for singles or couples generating minimal kitchen waste.

FoodCycler Eco 5.blurb: The most popular model with a 5-liter bucket. Designed for households of two to four people, offering fewer loading cycles per week.

Reencle Gravity.blurb: The more affordable Reencle option with 5-liter capacity. Retains core drying and grinding functionality without the smart odor sensor.

Reencle Prime.blurb: Premium Reencle model with 6-liter capacity, odor sensor for automatic cycle adjustment, and integrated carbon filter system.

ecobee Smart Thermostat.blurb: Smart thermostat with room sensors. I use it to monitor and optimize home energy usage — the energy reports show exactly where power is going.

Smart Plug Wi-Fi, Energy Monitoring.blurb: A smart plug with real-time energy monitoring. I track the wattage of individual devices to find hidden power drains.

Cree LED A19 Bulb, 60W, Soft White.blurb: LED bulbs that use a fraction of the power of incandescents. I've replaced every bulb in the house with these.

Window Insulation Shrink Kit.blurb: A cheap way to seal drafty windows in winter. The shrink film creates an insulating air gap that cuts heat loss.

Foam Weather Stripping.blurb: Self-adhesive foam strips for sealing gaps around doors and windows. Simple install, noticeable draft reduction.

Outlet Gaskets, Foam insulation.blurb: Foam gaskets that slip behind outlet and switch plates. Unsealed electrical boxes are a hidden source of drafts in exterior walls.

Smart Power Strip Wi-Fi, Energy Monitori.blurb: A smart power strip with individual outlet control and energy monitoring. I use it to kill phantom loads on entertainment centers and desk setups.

Low-Flow Showerhead.blurb: A low-flow showerhead that saves water without sacrificing pressure. One of the easiest upgrades for reducing household utility bills.
